reference.source: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology / Oxford Handbook of Endocrinology and Diabetes
clinicalPearls: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia caused by variants in HSD3B2
The type 2 enzyme is needed early in steroidogenesis to convert delta-5 to delta-4 steroids, so its loss impairs synthesis of mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids and potent androgens alike
The classic form causes salt wasting with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis, together with cortisol deficiency, and can precipitate adrenal crisis in the newborn period

Accumulated delta-5 steroids, especially dehydroepiandrosterone, are weak androgens, giving a characteristic pattern of undervirilisation in genetic males (ambiguous genitalia from partial androgen exposure) and mild virilisation such as clitoromegaly in some genetic females
The elevated ratio of delta-5 to delta-4 steroids (for example raised 17-hydroxypregnenolone) is the diagnostic biochemical hallmark
This is a salt-wasting, not hypertensive, form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, distinguishing it from the 11-beta and 17-alpha hydroxylase variants
Treatment combines glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement, with salt supplementation in infancy and sex-hormone support as needed
reference.pathophysiology: 3-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by variants in HSD3B2, encoding the type 2 isoenzyme that catalyses an early, shared step converting delta-5 steroids to delta-4 steroids in the adrenal and gonad. Because this step lies upstream of the mineralocorticoid, glucocorticoid and androgen branches, deficiency reduces aldosterone and cortisol production, leading to salt wasting with hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and metabolic acidosis and to cortisol insufficiency with risk of adrenal crisis. Loss of cortisol feedback raises ACTH and causes accumulation of delta-5 precursors such as dehydroepiandrosterone; these are only weak androgens, so genetic males are incompletely virilised while genetic females may show mild virilisation from peripheral conversion. The elevated delta-5 to delta-4 steroid ratio provides the biochemical signature, and unlike the hypertensive CAH variants there is no mineralocorticoid excess.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital adrenal hypoplasia and other causes of primary adrenal insufficiency
Other disorders of sex development causing ambiguous genitalia
additionalInvestigations: Adrenal steroid profile showing raised delta-5 steroids and an elevated delta-5 to delta-4 ratio (e.g. 17-hydroxypregnenolone)
Serum electrolytes demonstrating hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia and acidosis
Cortisol, ACTH, renin and aldosterone measurement
Karyotype and pelvic/gonadal imaging in ambiguous genitalia
redFlags: Neonatal salt-wasting adrenal crisis with severe hyperkalaemia and hypotension
Ambiguous genitalia requiring urgent multidisciplinary assessment
Circulatory collapse during intercurrent illness or under-replacement
reference.prognosis: With prompt glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid replacement and salt supplementation, the salt-wasting crises and cortisol deficiency can be managed and children grow well; long-term outcome depends on adherence, crisis prevention during illness, and appropriate management of the disorder of sex development.
pitfalls: Confusing it with 21-hydroxylase deficiency and misinterpreting the steroid profile
Failing to recognise that both males and females can have genital abnormalities (undervirilisation versus mild virilisation)
Missing impending adrenal crisis and not stress-dosing glucocorticoid during illness
Assuming a hypertensive CAH picture when this variant actually causes salt wasting
Overlooking the need for coordinated multidisciplinary care of ambiguous genitalia
references: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline on congenital adrenal hyperplasia
management: Replace glucocorticoid with hydrocortisone to correct cortisol deficiency and suppress excess ACTH.
Give mineralocorticoid replacement with fludrocortisone and sodium chloride supplementation to counter salt wasting.
Increase glucocorticoid cover during illness and treat salt-wasting adrenal crises urgently with parenteral hydrocortisone, fluids and correction of hyponatraemia and hyperkalaemia.
Monitor electrolytes, plasma renin, growth and adrenal steroid levels to titrate replacement.
Manage undervirilisation and atypical genitalia through a disorders-of-sex-development multidisciplinary team, with sex-steroid replacement to induce puberty as needed.
Provide genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance, with HSD3B2 testing and family screening.
